review.result:
## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR deletes `app/defaults.json`, and `load_defaults()` still reads that file, so startup breaks; this must be fixed before merge. `is_valid_port` rejecting port 65535 and `load_config` hiding read and parse errors should also be fixed.

## Changes
The PR adds millisecond parsing to `parse_timeout` and adds three new functions: `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (with an optional `ujson` accelerator) and `normalize_host`. It deletes `app/defaults.json`, adds a reviewer doc and a test fixture, and adds tests for the new paths.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json or update load_defaults — Every call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, because this PR deletes `app/defaults.json`. `app/startup.py:6` still runs `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`, and nothing else in the diff provides the `{"timeout":30}` default. — Any code path that loads application defaults crashes at startup.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 in is_valid_port — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, because `0 < p < 65535` excludes the upper bound. The docstring states the valid range as "1-65535", and `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` checks only 0, 1 and 8080. — Callers that validate config or user input will wrongly reject the highest valid TCP port. — Fix: `return 0 < p <= 65535`
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Stop returning {} for every load_config error — If the config path is missing, unreadable or holds malformed JSON (for example `{"timeout": 5,`), `load_config` returns `{}` with no log or signal. `except Exception` catches every error, and neither the docstring nor a comment says this fallback is intentional. No test exercises this path. — A broken config file silently runs the app on defaults, and operators have no clue why their settings were ignored. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` if a missing file should mean empty config, document that, and let parse errors propagate.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align normalize_host docstring with its empty return — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring says "returns None when h is empty", but line 37 runs `return ""`. — Callers that follow the docstring and check `is None` will treat an empty host as a valid normalized value.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Test the trailing-dot branch of normalize_host — No test passes a fully qualified host such as `"Example.COM."`, so the dot-stripping branch at lines 40-41 is never exercised. `test_normalize_host_lowercases` uses an input without a trailing dot. — A regression in trailing-dot handling would pass the test suite. — Fix: Extend `test_normalize_host_lowercases` with a trailing-dot input.
